## 📋 Summary This PR adds a client-side collapsible `AppSidebar` component that persists collapsed state in `localStorage` and subscribes to updates via `useSyncExternalStore`. While the subscription mechanism and active link matching are implemented cleanly, using `localStorage` with a static `getServerSnapshot` default causes a Flash of Expanded Content (layout shift) on SSR hydration, and collapsed navigation links lose their accessible names for screen readers. --- ## 🔍 Findings ### 🟠 High * **`hard_app_sidebar.tsx`:26-33** — **Hydration flash / layout shift (CLS) for collapsed users on SSR.** * *Failure path:* Because `localStorage` is inaccessible on the server, `getServerSnapshot()` hardcodes `"expanded"`. On initial page load for a user who previously collapsed the sidebar (`KEY === "1"`), the server renders the full expanded HTML. During client hydration, React renders expanded first, then immediately triggers a second client-only render to `"collapsed"`. This causes the sidebar and nav items to flash expanded and snap closed on every fresh page load, causing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). * *Fix:* Store layout-critical preferences in an HTTP cookie (e.g., read via `cookies()` in Next.js Server Components / middleware) so the server can render the correct initial state. If persisting strictly on the client, drive collapse styling purely through CSS rather than conditionally unmounting DOM elements (`{!collapsed && ...}`). --- ### 🟡 Medium * **`hard_app_sidebar.tsx`:62-65** — **Navigation links lose accessible name when sidebar is collapsed.** * *Failure path:* When `collapsed` is `true`, `{!collapsed && ...}` unmounts the text node, while `` is hidden from the accessibility tree. The link falls back solely to `title={item.label}`, which is inconsistently announced by screen readers and fails WCAG 2.1 (4.1.2 Name, Role, Value / 2.4.4 Link Purpose). * *Fix:* Always render the label in the DOM and toggle a visually hidden class (e.g., `sr-only`) when collapsed, or set `aria-label={item.label}` on ``: ```tsx {item.label} ``` --- ### 🟢 Low * **`hard_app_sidebar.tsx`:21, 36** — **Uncaught `DOMException` on restricted `localStorage` access.** * *Failure path:* In sandboxed iframes or private browsing modes with strict storage partitioning, calling `window.localStorage.getItem` or `setItem` can throw a `SecurityError` / `DOMException`, which will crash the snapshot reader during rendering. * *Fix:* Wrap `localStorage` access in a `try / catch`: ```ts function getSnapshot(): "collapsed" | "expanded" { try { return typeof window !== "undefined" && window.localStorage.getItem(KEY) === "1" ? "collapsed" : "expanded"; } catch { return "expanded"; } } ``` --- ## ✅ Positives * Snapshot getters (`getSnapshot`, `getServerSnapshot`) and the `subscribe` callback are declared at module scope, ensuring stable references for `useSyncExternalStore`. * Sub-route matching (`pathname === item.href || pathname.startsWith(item.href + "/")`) correctly prevents false positive matches on similarly prefixed sibling paths (e.g., `/settings-tab` matching `/settings`). * Good semantic HTML structure using `
